item.title: SCP-XXXX: Empathic Erhu (seeking greenlights)
item.description: A musical instrument that creates instantaneous empathy
item.content:encoded:
A musical instrument that creates instantaneous empathy, and the ethical/philosophical conflicts within the Foundation that result from it.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Mythological, Philosophical

Page Layout (Optional): Standard SCP layout with some tests and a few cross-tests

Elevator Pitch:

  • SCP-XXXX is an emotokinetic1 erhu that when played causes anyone who hears it to receive all of the emotions and underlying memories of the player.
  • SCP-XXXX achieves this "instantaneous empathy" by generating empathons, the elementary subatomic particle of the psychospace responsible for human emotion.2
  • SCP-XXXX can transmit any human emotion, resulting in a conflict between the O5 Council and the Ethics Committee concerning how best to use SCP-XXXX.

Central Narrative: SCP-XXXX is hand-delivered to the Foundation by the headless god of perseverance Xíng Tiān, who says that it will help humanity by bringing individuals together. Testing reveals that SCP-XXXX does this by using empathons to broadcast the emotions of the person playing SCP-XXXX.

+ show block
– hide block

However, because SCP-XXXX can use empathons to transmit any human emotion, a conflict arises between the O-5 Council, who want to weaponize SCP-XXXX, and the Ethics Committee, who want to use SCP-XXXX as a mode of communication with sapient SCP's.

This conflict is resolved when Xíng Tiān hijacks SCP-XXXX and gives all the D-class at Site-64 the ability to emotokinetically communicate with each other, allowing them to cooperate and pool their knowledge of certain SCP's to coordinate a prison break that leads to the loss of several SCP personnel.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: SCP-XXXX is an anomalous musical instrument that generates instantaneous empathy, and this emotokinetic ability results in an ethical conflict within the Foundation. SCP-XXXX also expands upon the lore of the psychospace and certain humanoid SCP's such as SCP-5027 and SCP-5278.

Additional Notes:

  • I know that Series I SCP's like SCP-187 and SCP-682 are fairly overdone; I would be happy to substitute them for more recent SCP's. Essentially, I need an SCP with precognitive abilities and an SCP that's physically invincible.
  • I read SCP-5027 a few weeks ago and loved the premise, although I did get bummed out by the ending. If the author of SCP-5027 is okay with it, I would like to use SCP-XXXX to give SCP-5027 a somewhat happier ending (nothing like leaving containment, but at least an ending where SCP-5027 can be treated like a human being).
  • Lastly, thank you for reading this SCP idea! Any guidance is much appreciated, and I look forward to hearing from you!

Collapsible edited as the post was still rather long. ~Zyn

Footnotes
1. capable of controlling the emotions of sentient beings
2. similar to the Higgs Boson being responsible for mass or the photon being responsible for light

item.title: [Seeking Greenlight] Unsolved Hypercube
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a Rubik's cube which, when close to being solved, begins to behave like a 4-dimensional Rubik's cube to prevent itself from being solved. When it nears being solved again it will instead begin to behave like a 5-dimensional Rubik's cube, and so on. After being far away enough from being solved it will revert to a lower dimension. These processes have a consistent order and pattern. As a byproduct SCP-XXXXs mass increases with each dimension over 3 dimensions it contains (starting with the mass of a regular Rubik's cube) as well as giving off a small amount of ionizing radiation. This increase in mass and the presence of radiation grows exponentially with each additional dimension.

Central Narrative: The central narrative of this piece would take the form of several testing logs where Dr. Cass experiments with SCP-XXXX and its unusual properties. Over time they work towards the possibility of using SCP-XXXXs radioactive properties for fuel in a power generator based on fusion reactor designs. This pursuit eventually leads to conflict with the site director who is against the idea. By the end of it the site director removes Dr. Cliff as the project lead (instead having them as a project advisor) and further experimentation with SCP-XXXX is delayed until a new project lead can be established.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The primary hook of this article is the mundane appearance of the anomaly in question. As people read it some might look at a Rubik’s cube they have (or a memory of it) which can draw them in closer. It's also a simple concept (a Rubik’s cube which prevents you from solving it) but goes very deep into the mechanics of the anomaly and such a concept actually works.

Additional Notes: None.

item.title: Super Turbo Laser Motorcarriage
item.description: A particularly dangerous MK II Toyota Supra
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Sci-Fi

Page Layout (Optional): I'm planning to add, to the usual stuff, a short log of the manhunt, three interviews with the driver and a test log - in that order.

Elevator Pitch: A MK II Supra. The faster it goes, the more universally degrading/degenerative its shell becomes - to the point where it can cut clean through practically anything. As a trade-off, it loses speed proportionally to damage done.

Central Narrative:
+ Central Narrative
- Hide

From the American midwest and moving south, a retired stuntman drives recklessly and attracts the police. In chases, he uses the car to his advantage - cutting through roadblocks and anything else that stands in his way. The Foundation is, of course, not very fond of this, and teams up with the FBI for a manhunt, which lasts 2 whole days and ultimately ends with a cleverly placed spike strip.

The old man is then brought in in a heavily intoxicated state, high on cocaine and MDMA. The three separate interviews are conducted within 1, 3 and 7 days inside his padded holding cell, which reveal the man's motivation to be a combination of forced retirement, an uneventful lifestyle and poverty. The straw that broke the camel's back was the death of his only friend, whose will provided him with the built black-on-yellow car. Realizing his life is already lived and not going to get better, the old man is overcome by rage and sadness. In that moment, he snaps and decides to go out with a bang - by buying copious amounts of drugs and embarking on a journey to the Californian West Coast, where he had once spent the brightest days of his youth.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The old man's story and interviews with a side serving of experiments conducted on the car.

Additional Notes: I'm debating, whether or not I should make the car's abilities wane over time as per active use.

The old man's friend knew of the anomalous properties, and kept it locked up in a rented garage out of fear and paranoia.

The car was first found left in the middle of his car lot one night.

item.title: [Seeking Greenlight] SCP article
item.description: SCP induces “autopilot”.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: yes

Page type: SCP article

Elevator pitch: SCP that steals the conscousness of random people, leaving their body on autopilot whilst their consciousness is put in a state of terror.

Central narrative: SCP-XXXX is an entity composed of a human head with oblong arms extending from where the ears should be. SCP-XXXX steals the victims consciousness for ascending time increments.

The victim’s body acts on “autopilot”, going about the day as normal. However, the body avoids conversation as much as possible and will simplify tasks to the furthest extent. For example, the body will make lunch for itself, but only the barest needs ie. It will take an apple and bottle of water instead of making use of an oven or stove.

It is unclear what happens to the consciousness when in SCP-XXXX’s control, as all memory is erased once the consciousness returns. However, once the consciousness has returned, the victim will feel large discomfort and disorientation at not being where they last remember being.

Hook: Attempts at communication show the entity to be slightly smarter than the average human. The creature claims to only want to show its victims what life could be like without having limitations in its realm of dreams. However, once subjects are exposed to the entity for extended periods, their body starts to meld with the floor until they cease existing altogether, from the minds of everyone. The only proof that they ever existed is written and video proof.

Additional notes: I am worried that this is very similar to other SCP’s but I cannot find any. Any critique will be helpful as well as suggestions on what to change.

item.title: SCP "Darkhouse" - [Seeking Greenlight]
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Terminal / SCP Historical

Page Layout (Optional): Discovery (audio recordings; scanned original documents; terminal)

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Perhaps there was a reason why the O5-Council decided to bury this information…

Elevator Pitch:
+ Open
- Close

A Junior Researcher logs onto an older terminal and uncovers a forgotten SCP with deep roots in the SCP foundations history.


Central Narrative:
+ Open
- Close

The SCP foundation has a questionable history, but this Junior Researcher attempts to solidify one of the oldest SCPs discovered by the Foundation. Compiling information from older terminals and transcribing paper archives, the SCP “Darkhouse” is reclassified as one of the earliest discovered SCPs. The SCP was “lost” when the Foundation transferred their data from paper to computers.

Dating back to 1792, the original Cape Henry Lighthouse was the first federally funded public works project of the newly formed United States government. In 1881, a new lighthouse was constructed to replace the original. With rising threats from around the world, both human and anomalous, the United States government attempted to utilize unexplainable properties the original lighthouse possessed.

The SCP “Darkhouse” ‘s anomalous properties are charged by UVA (315-400 nm) and UVB (280-315 nm) Ultraviolet radiation. The radiation appears to activate the anomalous properties, causing the SCP “Darkhouse” to enter an “active” state. During this state, the SCP “Darkhouse” will project a photon-absorbing substance, blocking all light it encompasses. Effects of the substance on living organisms have been redacted due to its tendencies to dissolve and dissipate matter. Containment procedures have been automated and the SCP “Darkhouse” has not been attended to by Foundation personnel since its original containment.


Additional Notes: “It doesn’t shine, it shadows…”

item.title: Uncertain Unreality
item.description: A person, who people think don't exist. Or is it nothing, that makes people think there's a person there?
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Psychological… something

Page Layout (Optional): A normal SCP article, but it's split into two distinct sections

Elevator Pitch: The SCP itself is more or less the designation for two separate scenarios. In scenario A, the SCP is a Euclid SCP, who's a young human girl, a bit distorted from reality, and makes half of the people who know of her think she doesn't actually exist.
In scenario B, the SCP is an infohazardous memetic effect, which makes half of the people who know of it think that there's a person there, who really isn't.
The memetic effect of either scenario is so powerful, and so overwhelming, that despite their best efforts, the foundation can't tell which one is true, so they've documented it as if it's neither and both at the same time.
After all, it's impossible to prove either way

Central Narrative: The main narrative is gonna come from how the scenario A SCP is mentally affected by her affliction, and how she may have gotten like this based on interviews with her and the like
Also, it's going to focus on how this uncertainty is affecting the foundation personnel who know of the SCP, including conflicts starting due to people in scenario A starting fights with people in scenario B
People are getting angry about a whole humanoid containment chamber which is going completely unused

Hook/Attention-Grabber: the main hook is obviously the esoterics of something that can't be proven to exist or not exist, and possibly how the foundation reacts to encountering something that they can't truly understand despite their best efforts. I'd imagine people would already be interested as soon as they see "Object Class: Euclid / Keter (?)"

Additional Notes: I guess above all else I want to know if this concept has been done before and if so I would like to know how to make it more unique.
Also, I just wanna know if it's good or not alltogether

item.title: Skeleton's Daycare
item.description: Just a skeleton taking care of some aliens.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: I don't really know, maybe a bit emotional in some parts?

  • Elevator Pitch
  • Central Narrative
  • Hook/Attention Grabber
  • Additional Notes

It's a daycare owned by a living skeleton. The skeleton itself isn't anomalous, it's just a normal human who decomposed into a skeleton but is still alive due to some immortality crystals on the walls of the daycare.

The only other people in the daycare are alien children. For the most part, they're fairly normal. They have a bit of a temper, and they're capable of causing minor earthquakes, so you might not wanna anger them too badly.

This daycare used to be pretty normal. Then these alien parents came in and had to drop their kids off because "they had to do something." When they left the kids at the daycare, they left them with some crystals that would make them and anyone near the crystals immortal.

Two people used to run the daycare, but the original owner left to go find the parents because they've been gone for way too long and they can't close without all the kids leaving. This left the other guy to run it all by himself, but the owner was out for so long that the other guy's body became a skeleton.

After some time, one of the alien parents came back and took their kid, along with one of the crystals. This caused the skeleton's life to become much harder. This, along with the stress of taking care of aliens, was adding up. Then more of the alien parents came in to take their kid and their crystal. It got worse and worse.

At some point, the skeleton couldn't take it anymore and just left the building, causing him to die from getting out of range from the crystals. The children were attached to him after living there for a long time, so they tried to bring him inside and get him to live again, but it didn't work. Remember in the Elevator Pitch how the kids could cause minor earthquakes? They're really upset now, and they're causing serious damage to the rest of the world. They tried calming them down, but nothing would work. Because of the danger, they had to put them into a comatose state and look for their parents quickly. It then ends with the Foundation contacting the original owner who explains that the rest of the parents are long gone. Neutralization was the only other option.

A daycare slowly going into ruins.

None.

item.title: Please don't stare
item.description: Blessings can, sometimes, become curses.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Drama/Emotional, History.

Page Layout (Optional): Probably a good chunk of the article will be filled with dialogues.

Elevator Pitch: a humanoid SCP cursed with a deadly beauty: anyone that makes eye contact cannot feel happiness after that, slowly losing the will to live. The physical aspect of the SCP is different for each person.

Central Narrative: This being would be discovered when the suicide rate of a small town began to show astronomic growth. When brought to the foundation site, a scientist would open the eyes and bring a curse to 5 foundation personnel. The SCP would cooperate with the foundation to try and find a solution, but no amnestics would work and the five would eventually die of starvation or commit suicide, leaving the SCP crying on the corner of it’s cell. Following this tragic event, a series of cold-hearted tests would be performed, including sending many D-class personnel to stare at it’s eyes. The O-5 council decided to shut down the tests for being “too cruel” and the tests would now only be performed in case of someone accidentally staring the creature.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Testing on the SCP would show superhuman strength and resistance, as well as high knowledge in diverse areas and an extensive vocabulary, including many different languages. The SCP would have its own personality, portrayed by the “logs” of his conversation between the scientists, and it loves someone to read a book to it. This SCP is a pacifist, knocking out the opponents instead of killing them (this would be proven in the few containment breaches of his).

Additional Notes: I hadn’t come with a cool name yet. Also, if anyone finds an existing SCP with a similar concept, please notify.

item.title: Seeking Greenlight for first SCP: True NPC
item.description: Self aware NPC attempts to break out to the real world
item.content:encoded:
Self aware NPC attempts to break out to the real world, after Foundation tries to contain it, and learns about multi-layered nature of the Foundation reality, created specifically to stop pataphysical threats (Copied elevator pitch)

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): (meta) Horror

Page Layout (Optional): Two variants of the article, one describing the SCP upon discovery and initial tests, the other after learning about it's true scope

Elevator Pitch: Self aware NPC attempts to break out to the real world, after Foundation tries to contain it, and learns about multi-layered nature of the Foundation reality, created specifically to stop pataphysical threats

Central Narrative: Foundation learns about the existence of a self aware character from roleplaying games, whose name is a cognitohazard, that forces people perceiving it to include this character in their roleplaying activities. They try to contain it, like any other memetically spreading SCP, but it did not want to have its freedom restricted, so it decided to break out to the real world. Foundation, prepared for this kind of pataphysical dangers, created beforehand many layers of fictional realities, each identical to the top one, with Earth, Foundation and all the jazz, to contain entities traveling upwards through layers of fictional realities.

+ show block
– hide block

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Afaik there are no skips going "upwards'' through the reality layers, besides SCP-3812, who accidently went from our reality one level higher, but we don't have any coming from "below" and on purpose. Similarly, there is a multitude of fictional (from the in-universe point of view) SCPs but not much connected to the roleplaying (books and computer games get the majority of attention in this area afaik). I'm also planning on exploring limits of the mentioned cognitohazard, and the entity itself through test logs (something I see rather rarely, but find personally fascinating).

Additional Notes: English is not my first language (as you can probably tell) and I'll be thankful for pointing any misspellings or grammar mistakes. Also I never before used any »real« internet forum more complicated than facebook or reddit, so I'm sorry in advance for my mistakes while trying to make sense of it (I hope that I created this post in the right way). Thanks for reading, I hope you will like my idea, and maybe I'll manage to get the greenlight for my first SCP ^^


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

item.title: A Simple Bar
item.description: serving drinks to all dimensions!
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Mystery/Horror

Page Layout (Optional): Interview logs and also a log about when the bar manifested and when the Foundation sent an MTF in to determine if the place is a threat

Elevator Pitch: A "simple" bar and owner of said bar, that has the ability to hop across dimensions in order to serve as many customers as possible. Said bar
sets up shop just outside a Foundation site in the middle of nowhere in the hopes of making more money.

Central Narrative:
+Block
-Block

The bartender and owner is relatively open and talkative about the people he's met and places he's been, but when the foundation start trying to find out
some of the more personal questions about his and the bars history he starts getting more dismissive and less talkative. My idea is that the Owner used to run the place with his brother until they traveled to a dimension they weren't welcome in, with the consequence being that the brother is kept half dead, bloody, and basically soulless chained up in the back room of the bar. The owner is unable to let his brother die and let himself move on, so he pays the strange man who lives in the dimension a fee every month for him to help keep his brother alive. In an attempt to make as much money as he can to pay the strangers increasing demands he puts his bar down next to a very busy Foundation site. The interviews with foundation staff start fine with the owner happily telling stories and chatting, but each interview he gets more and more reserved and disturbed with hints and clues as to his brothers fate, until just before an interview the owner comes out from the backroom with blood on his hands with tears in his eyes.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: What I'm trying to go for is it starting all happy with stories and fun banter and slowly see it turn into horror.

Additional Notes: I plan on leaving most of the history of the place only hinted at so the reader could speculate and come to their own conclusions.

item.title: An in-depth report into the structure of the Foundation.
item.description: A tale idea which will take the style of a report
item.content:encoded:
A tale idea which will take the style of a report explaining the the highest levels of the SCP Foundation.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: Tale

Genre: Factual, Informative

Page Layout: Report title and brief summary of purpose, note from report's author, tier explanation, 05 council, ethics committee, administrator, general high level staff

Elevator Pitch: A report commissioned by the 05 council simplifying and explaining how the different branches of the SCP Foundation interact and their relevant powers and duties. item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout: Fairly heavy test log.

Elevator Pitch: The SCP is a gun store named ‘Gun-thers Armory’ owned by '(Name Pending. Maybe MC&D.)'. It has all the amenities you would expect (Firing Room, Break Room, etc). It is open at almost all hours, closing at 23:30 on Saturday, and reopening at 0:00 on Sunday. Every time the store is reopened, there will be 1 firearm inside a glass case that is anomalous. The glass case will not restock until the store closes and reopens. It also has some other minor anomalous properties, such as an indestructible shooting gallery, a fridge in the break room that always has some food in it (even if it was previously empty).

Central Narrative: After finding several anomalous arms throughout the local area, the foundation traces the guns back to the store. They investigate the store under the guise of “Safety Inspectors”. They attempt to shut down, buy out, or overall, limit public action, but every time they try, within a few hours, it is reverted. This is found to be due to the fact that the company has a seemingly endless supply of funds and resources. They investigate the place’s 1 worker who works there for the entire time (anomalously severe case of insomnia lets him work all week.). The guy considers it as irrelevant to talk about his job outside of work, so the foundation just puts a mic on their glasses to monitor them. As for the store itself, the foundation try to make the minor anomalies seem normal to the public, and just buy the anomalous gun the second the store opens. There will be test logs for the weapons. MTFs are allowed to use any weapons created, excluding those deemed unsafe for usage by the ethics committee, those ineffective for what the foundation requires from their weaponry, or those who have too minor an effect to replace standard issue weaponry. Eventually, the foundation shuts down the store by just demolishing it. They have to relocate the firing range.

These shadows form in place of normal shadows, but once manifesting, can only be removed if a deer heart is cast into it. When any mammalian matter, live or dead, passes into the shadow, it is devoured at a rapid rate by numerous small, unseen entities. If this occurs, and a deer heart is not fed to the shadow within 5 minutes, the instance will spontaneously grow to a much larger size until it is fed a deer heart.

Central Narrative: First began occurring in the Massacre Rim Dark Sky Sanctuary, Nevada, before spreading to the nearby 100 kilometres, including a Foundation site. The deer heart protocol was discovered when a deer ran into an instance and it disappeared. The Foundation then discovers that during a solar eclipse, the into 100 kilometre area will become one massive instance, killling everyone inside. A final addendum implied that its area of influence is growing.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Focusses on the very common fear of the dark and what may lurk inside. Furthermore, there is the implication that it is growing, and a solar eclipse may one day threaten an end of the world scenario.

Additional Notes: It is inspred by the Aztec Goddess Itzpapalotl, so there are reasons behind the deer heart and the solar eclipse.

item.title: The Unneeded Pact of Fire

item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout (Optional): The main meat of the SCP would be mainly within a journal written by SCP-XXXX-01

Elevator Pitch: This SCP consists of 3 entities: SCP-XXXX would be a chiminea outside a town in Alaska that can only be lit with human remains. SCP-XXXX-01 would be tied to the chiminea and lure people into lighting a fire in the pot and adding their bodies as fuel. If the fire is not lit for a set amount of time, SCP-XXXX-02 will appear out of the nearest lit flame and drag the closest human into the flame, resetting the clock.

Central Narrative: The bulk of the article would be in the form of a journal written by SCP-XXXX-01 revealing the history of SCP-XXXX and why the fire needs to be lit. The previously mentioned town was struggling during the first winter after settling, fires wouldn’t stay lit and people were freezing. A woman (SCP-XXXX-01) leaves to get supplies for the town, and when returning notices the SCP Foundation has descended on the settlement. She sees the Foundation as the “bad guys”, and eventually makes a deal with SCP-XXXX to allegedly get rid of the Foundation in the area and save her town and family from the harsh winter. This ties her to SCP-XXXX, and she is now charged with keeping the fire lit and SCP-XXXX-02 at bay.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The SCP would have been a Safe classification if not for civilian interference. I think it would be interesting to explore the idea of an SCP realizing they have unwittingly doomed themselves and made matters worse trying to save others. SCP-XXXX-01 would watch and document her family moving on without her, and the town expand and advance to the point where a deal to save the town from a harsh winter isn’t needed anymore, but the deal remains.

Additional Notes: My one fear is not getting a good enough connection/back-and-forth between SCP-XXXX and SCP-XXXX-01 to make the deal appealing enough to take, but that’s a bridge to cross in the draft stage. Also the title can use some critique as well.

item.title: SCP idea: CODE NAME: T.T.P
item.description: Just an SCP idea. This SCP is in very very early development.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking greenlights: no

Page type: SCP concept

Elevator pitch:
SCP code name: T.T.P

T.T.P is a humanoid who is covered in long, thick, black hair, this hair seems to be unaffected by gravity.

T.T.P has a plush toy which it refuses to let go of, it is extremely protective of this plush toy.

T.T.P is extremely tall, around 9 feet tall.

T.T.P has large marble like green eyes which are incapable of blinking.

T.T.P will not physically harm anyone unless its plush toy is touched or it hears an extremely loud noise. If T.T.Ps toy is touched they will go into a fit of rage and brutally attack whoever touched it. If T.T.P hears an extremely loud noise it will be extremely aggressive towards anyone it sees for the next 10 minutes. No one has ever been recorded to have survived one of T.T.Ps attacks.

T.T.P is childlike when it is not aggressive. When presented with toys it will normally begin to play with said toys. If given crayons they will begin to scribble on the walls. It seems to be very much entertained by such activities.

T.T.P sheds hair gradually over the course of months. shed hairs are quickly replaced by new hairs furthermore shed hairs continue to be unaffected by gravity. Direct physical exposure to a shed hair from T.T.P causes exposed subjects to experience terrifying hallucinations of T.T.P, subjects commonly have 5-6 hallucinations per day and normally never stop experiencing them, there seems to be no way to reverse the effects of exposure.

Direct physical contact with T.T.P causes the exposed subject to immediately become terrified of seemingly everything, the subject with normally kill themselves in the next few days. Yet again there seems to be no way to reverse the effects of exposure.

Central narrative:
T.T.P was discovered by accident while the INFORMATION CLASSIFIED was conducting a mission to plan a possible way to extract the Titanic from the Atlantic ocean. A submersible vehicle which has been given the name Seacat (which was being piloted by Cpt. Gala Smyth and copiloted by Dr. Thomas Snow) was using a device to digitally map out weak points in the sunken ship when an extremely odd shape was picked up within the ship.

Curious to discover what was being picked up by the device Cpt. Gala Smyth ejected a mini RC submersible from the Seacat. Dr. Thomas Snow then proceeded to steer the mini sub towards a small breach on the ship as to enter the vessel.

After a few minutes of searching different rooms Dr. Snow spotted something which made their stomach sink and their hair stand on end; a tall, black, linky figure stood motionless in the corner of a desolate room which was being poorly illuminated by the flash light on the mini sub.

Cpt. Smyth soon noticed Dr. Snow staring at the monitor with a horrified look on his face. She jokingly punched the doctors shoulder, asking him if he'd seen a ghost but the smile was soon ripped off her face as she turned her attention to the image on the monitor. Her jaw dropped. She stared at the figure, trying to make sense of it.

Cpt. Smyth soon swallowed her fear and regained her composure before shaking Dr. Snows shoulder and telling him to pilot the mini submersible out of the ship and back to the Seacat. Silently the doctor nodded his head and did as requested before Cpt. Smyth piloted her sub to the surface, shivering every now and then at the thought of the creature they had spotted.

The company was informed of their discovery and the SCP foundation was soon called in. The company was INFORMATION SECRET as to ensure that they kept quiet about the discovery.

Hook/attention grabber:
I think that my concept is fairly interesting due to the very odd looks of this SCP and the odd combination of childlike innocence and brutal aggression. I also think that the location in which this SCP was discovered is quite odd and allows people to speculate what it was doing there.

Additional notes: please keep in mind that this SCP is still in very early development and that this is also my first ever attempt at actually creating an SCP. I really want to know if this concept has potential and where or how it can be improved. If you really like this concept then I will continue to develop it and some day see if I can get it green lit, if you don't like it then I'll scrap it and start a different concept.

item.title: Seeking Greenlight - The Tontine Tree
item.content:encoded:
Hello, I am seeking a greenlight for my SCP proposal.

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Mystery

Page Layout: SCP article in progress to allow the reader to see the Foundation's progression in understanding an SCP.

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a tree. When touched by a living entity, a crude tattoo of an 'M' appears on its forehead, marking it as a contestant in a game. In addition, a portion of the contestant's lifespan will be taken away, physically aging the contestant. When there is only one living contestant left, they receive all of the life taken by the tree.

Central Narrative: The wizard who created the tree wants the process to end because he too is a player. Unfortunately, the Foundation discovers the tree at around this time.

When the Foundation discovers the tree, they observe only it ages living things that touch it and conclude that is the extent of its anomalous properties. However, the subjects that have touched the tree are kept on site to find any long term effects of exposure. When strange events occur on base, they are attributed to the tree but are actually the effect of the wizard breaking into the site and killing test subjects.

Following revisions will include further testing as a result of the new 'phenomenon'. A parallel effort is made to search the surrounding area for animals effected by the SCP to investigate long term effects of the SCP. However, when they find animals effected by the SCP are dying of natural causes AND the that they die only when being quarantined in the site, they suspect a third party.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: A small Foundation facility tries to fix their flawed understanding of an SCP while being sabotaged by an unknown entity.

Additional Notes: 

The article can end two ways: the wizard is caught and a potentially humorous interview begins.
Alternatively, the Foundation can find concrete evidence the wizard exists but he remains at large.

Thank you for your time. I would appreciate any feedback you may have.

[Edit Jan 4, 2020 - Idea fleshed out, thanks to JamaisJ]

item.title: Seeking greenlight for my idea: The fibonacci watch
item.description: Revised idea of my original SCP idea. Seeking greenlights and feedback.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror/Mystery

Page Layout: Standard layout, including a picture of the watch, interviews and testing.

Elevator Pitch: When wearing this watch, all sequences of numbers will become the Fibonacci code. All numbers change in the wearers eyes to be in the sequence of 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13 and so on. The wearer will also only be able to complete mathematic equations including the Fibonacci code. Images or paintings including faces will also turn into the face of Fibonacci.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: The central narrative of this SCP will be revealed throughout a series of interviews and tests. The first interview is with the original owner of this SCP, now named SCP-XXXX-A. SCP-XXXX-A is a human male, approximately 1.7m in height. His personality is described as “Partially paranoid and curious.” During his interview, SCP-XXXX-A, who originally owned the watch before it was acquired by the foundation, will describe it as "A comfortable item of clothing I used to wear." They will state that after purchasing it from a local garage sale in █████, they did not notice anything strange until a few days after, when they wore it for the first time. They will say that numbers in their life started to change rapidly, and he could no longer do basic equations other than those in the Fibonacci code. He will then state that when visiting an art museum with his family while wearing the watch, all self-portraits and paintings including faces turned into the face of Fibonacci. He also noted that in real life, people's faces did not change to that of Fibonacci. Finally, the man will state that after 5 consecutive days of wearing the watch, he began to become terrified of the watches power and decided to call the police. The police did not care about the man's concerns as they did not believe him, but the foundation later contained SCP-XXXX-A and SCP-XXXX during a raid of SCP-XXXX-A's house.

The second section of narrative will be a series of tests performed by a Dr. █████. The first test will be a test to see if the SCP can make any form of image of a face transform into Fibonacci's. A D-Class personnel will be given 3 copies of the same image. One will be a digital .png file, one will be printed onto paper and one shall be an artist's renditioning of the image. After wearing the watch for 10 minutes with the images in front of them, the D-Class will then be asked if the faces in each image changed to that of Fibonacci. The D-Class will state that yes, all faces became Fibonacci’s. The second test was conducted on a D-Class that had previously been a mathematician before being contained at Site-██. This test included the D-Class wearing the watch while solving multiple simple equations. The first 12 equations that the D-Class solved were done with general ease, however, after this point, the D-Class seemed to struggle with solving further equations. When asked why, the D-Class simply stated, “It’s Fibonacci. It’s all Fibonacci.” The third and final test was conducted using SCP-5755 (http://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/scp-5755) A D-Class personnel was given 4 images while wearing SCP-XXXX, all the images being of SCP-5755's “sources”. The D-Class is then asked to say the numbers in the sources, and gives the output, “112358, 132134, 558914, 423337”. They are then asked to shuffle the papers and once again say the numbers in the sources. The D-Class only repeats the same numbers they originally stated. These are of course the beginning numbers of the Fibonacci code in sequential order, and not the correct source numbers.

Hook/Attention Grabber: It's a watch that tells time in Fibonacci code, displays numbers in the Fibonacci code and overall changes the wearers mind into that of a pure follower of Fibonacci and his sequence.

Additional Notes: This is a very detailed SCP, and I have done my best to include each detail that I would like to be put into the final article in this greenlighting pitch. All feedback is also welcome. Thanks!

THIS IS VERSION 2

item.title: Labeling an SCP and determining its Object Class
item.description: Trying to figure out the Object Class for an SCP that sorta contains more than one SCP. I don't really know how to explain it quickly.
item.content:encoded:
Just some notes before I get into it:
1. Not entirely sure I am putting this thread in the right place since I have never posted on here before. If it is in the wrong place, I am sorry and could you please direct me to the right place?
2. I am not looking for a critique on the SCP I am writing. It is extremely unlikely that I will ever post the page for the SCP because I have no confidence and I just like writing these for fun.

I have two questions I need answers and one may answer the other.
Here is the situation. What I am going to refer to as SCP-X is a large sphere-shaped object that can be used to open a dimensional portal. SCP-Y is a sentient being that has come through the portal from the other dimension. SCP-Y is the only known being that has crossed over. The Foundation does not know if there are more beings on the other side because the portal closed again before they could explore it, and they do not know how to reopen it. SCP-Y has no connection to SCP-X aside from coming through the portal opened up by SCP-X. With that in mind, would the two be kept in the same SCP entry?
If the answer is no, then ignore the rest of this. If the answer is yes, I have another question.
SCP-X is considered Safe. Just build a structure around it (since it is too big to move) and it won't do anything. SCP-Y is Euclid. It is a sentient and sapient being that needs the same basic needs as a human. It also does not like to be contained and may try and break out, but none of its abilities really make it any harder to contain than a normal human. If SCP-X and SCP-Y were to be under the same entry, what would the Object Class at the top of the entry be?

Thanks for any help.

item.title: SCP Idea: The Loneliest Goddess
item.description: There's a god or goddess for everything- how about a goddess of atheists?
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights:Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Comedy

Elevator Pitch:

A goddess referring to itself as the Matrem Obliviscetur, or Forgotten Mother, who is the Goddess of Atheists. It derives its power from disbelief, so the fewer people who know of its existence, the more power it gains. However, it suffers from a paradox of belief: Because it is benevolent, it wishes to help atheists by answering their prayers. However, since atheists lack belief in gods, they never make requests. This has made it extremely powerful, but it has limited ways to exercise this, being resigned to giving its followers "gifts" of luck or small boons, which more often than not hurt the recipient more than help.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: A series of discovery logs tell the Foundation's unwitting discovery of the Matrem posing as human in order to be closer to its followers. A series of interviews with the Matrem by various researchers bring to light its origins and its clear depression. Subsequent experiments are conducted where it is encouraged to interact with several atheist D-class personnel, over the course of which its depression only worsens, and it is discovered that the Matrem's emotions affect a wide-ranging area, causing the inhabitants of nearby regions to become despondent. In order to prevent further damage, the Foundation provides a solution for the Matrem by which it is provided with subjects who are made aware of its existence and make a request of it, and then given amnestics in order to wipe their memories of the encounter, making them eligible to receive the aid.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The idea of a god that exists for no reason, as a sort of reversal of the idea that life is meaningless and has no purpose, as experienced by an immortal whose very purpose cannot be fulfilled

item.title: Greenlight SCP - omniscient
item.description: What would happen if humans knew anything?
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes.

Page Type: SCP Article.

Elevator Pitch: Humans learn things throughout life. But, what if they born with all the knowledge?

Central Narrative: This scp is an eleven-year-old human boy who appears to know all the things in the universe. He can also tell the date and time of someone's birth, and the date, time, and how someone will die. At first, everyone thought he sees the future, but he denied it, and said he only knew.

He has big brown eyes and hair of the same color. According to research done, he looks like a normal boy from the inside out.

The organization managed to reach him through a call that the scp himself made. Follow the call below:

//SCP: Hi, am i talking to Dr. XXXXX of the SCP foundation?

Dr. XXXX: Yes …. Wait, how do you know that kind of information?

SCP: I know many things, come and get me, i am waiting.//

+ show block
– hide block

Hook/Attention-Grabber: A kid who knows everything.

Additional Notes: This scp refused to answer certain questions, such as "When will the world end?" or "Is there really a God?", or even the source of his knowledge. His statement was that answering these questions could put humanity at risk.

He knows how to do things like painting, cooking, playing instruments. He seems to have all the talents imaginable. Once he sang for a group of employees, everyone left delighted.

The organization tried to use him to acquire information from other scp's, but he refused to give it by saying that he should not interfere in this type of thing.

He can speak all languages, even the ones that aren't human.

He can walk freely around the organization.

He has already helped employees to repair machines and even communicated with scp's with different languages than a normal human.

He is not a affected by SCP-035, it looks like he can't be manipulated.

item.title: The Laughing Tree
item.description: Greenlight? A tree manipulates children into hazing one of their own, leading to suicides. Survivors can only laugh.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Campfire Horror, Emotional

Page Layout (Optional): Containment procedure, description of the entity's feeding ritual, 2 interviews with a survivor of the ritual, and 1 interview with an involved camp staff-member.

Elevator Pitch: The Laughing Tree is a memetic entity rooted within an old wooden-tent campground commonly used by scouts or youth groups. The tree convinces children to tie one of their own to its trunk, upon which they are mentally scarred. Many of these children later runaway from home, but some of them return to the tree, carve their name in its trunk and kill themselves. Any mention of the tree, the tying, or the deaths are brushed off with casual laughter.

Central Narrative: A low-level foundation member calls attention to this entity after his child is almost tied to the tree. Previously, he laughed the tale off as a "camp story" to several co-workers. He is told to bring in his child for questioning.

+ show block
– hide block

The first interiew is short. After providing a cover story, the investigator asks what happened. Emotionally dead, the kid replies, "you'll just laugh at me.."

The second interview occurs after the parent tries to console their child. The parent tries to help answer preliminary questions by describing camp activities. At the mention of knot-tying, the child's face goes pale.

The interviewer asks why the child didn't want to attend camp. Instead of answering he makes a small digression about how he felt sorry for a spider that another kid burned. The parent interrupts and describes his child as socially isolated and wonders if this behavior is related to the nature of his work.

Eventually, the child describes what happened, One-by-one belongings of other scouts find their way to his tent. Camp staff approach him and ask about thefts. The child tries to explain that he didn't take them, but they laugh at him. He runs. Then they, the scouts, surround him with knot-tying ropes and force him toward the *tree*. He tries and fails to escape, as the scouts laugh at him. The laughter grows louder.. and deeper until he realizes that it's coming from behind. And then, the laughter stops.

The investigator asks what changed. The child looks down, and cries.

A third interview takes place with a camp staff-member and witness. He laughs at the hazing and the deaths, "Why should I feel sorry for a bunch of thieves?"

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Laughter, not as a coping mechanism but as something to be feared.

Additional Notes: Besides names, the tree also has "LOL" etched into its bark, and it is disgusted by urine.

  • Give it to a Rubik-solving robot, have it running 24-7 and record everything with a camera. Use it as a true source of entropy for an SCP-owned secure communications channel

Additional Notes: it's supposed to be a tongue-in-cheek SCP that could be useful to the Foundation (not quite Thaumiel).
